A simple electrolytic cell. A glass beaker containing a blue solution (electrolyte) with two carbon rods dipping into it. Wires connect the top of the rods to a DC battery and a switch. The left rod is connected to the positive terminal") and the right rod to the negative terminal"). Negative ions in the solution have arrows pointing to the anode, and positive ions have arrows pointing to the cathode.

Diagram of electroplating a spoon. A glass beaker containing a solution of silver salt (AgNO3). A bar of pure silver is connected to the positive terminal (anode). A metal spoon is connected to the negative terminal (cathode). Arrows show Ag+ ions moving from the silver bar through the solution to coat the spoon.
